summary.description: Two or three sentences: what the PR does and your overall verdict.

findings.description: One entry per distinct defect. Empty array if the PR is clean.

id.description: Sequential id using the prefix you were given, e.g. CC-1, CC-2.

title.description: Under 80 characters. The claim alone, no rationale.

severity.description: blocking = you would hold the merge for it. Must agree with action: blocking implies fix-before-merge.

action.description: Whether it is worth the author's time now, weighing deployment context: flag state, code already scheduled for deletion, deferrals the PR itself documents. A real defect on a dead path is fix-later or nit.

introduced_by_pr.description: yes = this PR creates the defect; worsened = it existed but this PR makes it more reachable or more harmful; no = pre-existing and untouched in effect.

posting_line.description: A line of `file` in the PR head that lies inside a changed hunk of diff.patch, where an inline review comment can anchor: `line` itself when it is in a hunk, else the nearest changed line in the same file that leads to it. 0 when no changed line in `file` relates to it.

line.description: 1-indexed line in the PR head revision. Use 0 only if genuinely file-wide.

symbol.description: Enclosing function/class/constant name, or "" if none.

failure_scenario.description: Concrete inputs or state, then the wrong output/crash/leak that results. Not a generalization.

evidence.description: file:line references plus quoted code that proves the claim. Cite every file you relied on, including ones outside the diff.

suggested_fix.description: The smallest change that resolves it.
